target_body: Promotional pricing lifted new accounts by 31% and booked revenue by 18% among price-sensitive buyers, though renewals fell by 12 points at the first term; the billing plan mix stayed constant.
system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.
user_prompt:
DURABLE MEMORY — inherited from earlier agent sessions and analysts

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived
    Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived
    Promotional pricing lifted new accounts by 31% and booked revenue by 18% among price-sensitive buyers, though renewals fell by 12 points at the first term; the billing plan mix stayed constant.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

memory_block.body: Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.
Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.
Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.
Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.
Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.
Promotional pricing lifted new accounts by 31% and booked revenue by 18% among price-sensitive buyers, though renewals fell by 12 points at the first term; the billing plan mix stayed constant.

answer.rationale:
The observed damage is upstream funnel decay (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%), not a pricing problem per se, so the highest-leverage single slot is the onboarding/activation path rather than a price response to the competitor. memory_73 is the decisive negative case: promotional pricing bought a 31% account lift and 18% booked revenue while renewals dropped 12 points at first term, which is a direct hit to sustainable long-term qualified revenue and exactly the trap of chasing an entry-price competitor. memory_44 (enterprise sales-assist) and memory_57 (referrals in established customers) address different segments than the leaking SMB/self-serve funnel, so they do not fit this week's deficit.

I am spending verification on memory_86 and memory_91 because they are the two live candidates for this slot and both are compressed in a way that hides the metric that matters. memory_86 reports completion rate and time-to-value, and memory_31 reports first-week activation "durable lift" — both are upper-funnel proxies. Neither summary states whether the accounts that were pushed through a shortened flow retained or generated qualified revenue. That is precisely the failure shape memory_73 documented: a real top-line lift that concealed downstream value destruction. Cutting required fields or steps can also strip out qualification and expectation-setting, importing lower-intent accounts and degrading lead quality. So I want the original records to see (a) whether retention/revenue was measured at all or only assumed, (b) the segment and baseline, and (c) how much of memory_86 is just a restatement of memory_31 rather than independent evidence. I pull memory_91 rather than memory_31 as the second because activation messaging is the fallback lever if the onboarding record turns out to rest on proxies alone, and because memory_86 and memory_31 likely share the same underlying test.

I am committing to a standard experiment, not a broad rollout, with retention and qualified-revenue guardrails read at first renewal rather than at week-one completion. If verification shows memory_86 never tracked downstream value, I will narrow to a small guarded test or pivot to activation_messaging, which changes in-product guidance without removing qualification friction and therefore carries less downstream risk. Stated intent is provisional pending the archive pulls.
